Horsemen sent to Najd bring Thumama bin Uthal, chief of Yamama, who is tied to a pillar of the mosque until the Prophet orders his release.
Ka'b, arguing loudly with his debtor, is told by the Prophet's gesture to drop half the debt, and he takes half.
Al-As bin Wail will not repay Khabbab unless he rejects Muhammad, saying he will pay after resurrection with property and offspring, and a verse is revealed about such a man.
Found things are announced for a year, then used but returned if the owner comes; lost sheep are taken, camels left; a lender finds his money in driftwood.
The Prophet would have eaten a date fallen on the road, or on his bed, but for fear it was from Sadaqa.
Mecca's thorny bushes, game and grass are protected, except Idhkhir, and its fallen things may be picked up only to announce them; the speech is written for Abu Shah.
No one should milk another's animal without its owner's permission, for udders are their owners' stores, as no one would want his storeroom broken into.
A found thing is announced for a year, its container and string remembered, and returned if its owner comes; Ubai announced a found purse for up to three years.
Abu Bakr has a Quraishi's shepherd milk a sheep, cools the milk by pouring water over its covered pot, and the Prophet drinks till Abu Bakr is pleased.
Believers settle wrongs among themselves on a bridge before Paradise; Allah screens a believer, has him confess his sins and forgives them, while disbelievers and hypocrites are exposed.
A Muslim is a Muslim's brother, neither oppressing him nor handing him to an oppressor; help your brother, oppressor or oppressed, by stopping his oppression; believers are like a building.
Oppression will be darkness on Resurrection Day, an oppressed person's curse has no screen before Allah, and an oppressor should seek pardon now or repay in good deeds and sins.
Aisha says verse 4.128 concerns a man who dislikes his wife and means to divorce her, and she gives up her rights so that he keeps her.
Given a drink, the Prophet asks the boy on his right to let the old men have the rest, but the boy declines, so he hands him the bowl.
Whoever unjustly takes even a span of another's land will have it encircling his neck down the seven earths, or will sink down them, on the Day of Resurrection.
The Prophet forbade eating two dates at a time without one's companions' permission, and asks Abu Shu'aib's permission for an uninvited man who followed him to the meal.
The most quarrelsome is most hated by Allah; the Prophet, being human, may mistakenly rule for the more eloquent party, and what is wrongly given is a portion of Fire.
Whoever lies when he speaks, breaks his promises, betrays covenants and is insulting in quarrels is a hypocrite, and one of these traits is a trait of hypocrisy.
Hind may feed her children from the property of Abu Sufyan, whom she calls a miser, if she does so justly and reasonably.
Companions the Prophet sends out may accept due hospitality from their hosts, and take a guest's right from those who refuse it.
When the Prophet died, the Ansar assembled in the shed of Bani Sa'ida, and Umar and Abu Bakr went to them.
No one should stop his neighbour fixing a wooden peg in his wall, Abu Huraira narrates despite his hearers' reluctance.
When alcohol is prohibited, Anas spills Abu Talha's wine into Medina's streets, and a verse says believers who did good are not blamed for what they consumed before.
Those who must sit on the roads are to give the road its rights: lowering the gaze, not harming people, returning greetings, and enjoining good and forbidding evil.
A man who climbed down a well to water a thirsty dog was forgiven, as serving any living being earns reward.
From a high building in Medina the Prophet says he sees afflictions falling among their houses as thickly as raindrops.
Umar names Aisha and Hafsa as the two wives in verse 66:4 and tells how the Prophet kept away from his wives twenty-nine days, then offered them a choice.
Jabir brings the camel to the mosque, telling the Prophet it is his, and the Prophet, after examining it, says both the camel and its price are Jabir's.
The Prophet came to some people's rubbish dump and urinated there standing.
Allah thanked and forgave a man who removed a thorny branch from the road.
In a dispute about land the Prophet ruled that seven cubits be left as a public way.
The Prophet forbade robbery and mutilation, and said an adulterer, a drinker of alcohol, a thief or a robber is not a believer while committing the act.
The Hour will not come before the son of Mary descends as a just ruler, breaks the cross, kills the pigs and abolishes the jizya, and money abounds unaccepted.
At Khaibar the Prophet ordered the pots cooking donkey meat to be emptied and broken, then allowed them to be washed instead.
Entering Mecca, the Prophet struck the three hundred and sixty idols around the Ka'bah with a stick, reciting that truth has come and falsehood has vanished.
The Prophet tore Aisha's curtain decorated with pictures, and she made it into two cushions that he sat on.
Whoever is killed while protecting his property is a martyr.
When one wife broke a bowl of food sent by another, the Prophet gathered the food, kept the broken bowl and sent back an unbroken one.
Juraij, an Israelite, ignored his mother's call while praying; she prayed he would see prostitutes' faces, a woman claimed her baby was his, and the baby named the shepherd.
Short of food, Abu Ubaida's army and the Ash'aris pooled their provisions and shared them equally, the Prophet blessed a pooled heap, and a camel's meat was split ten ways.
